mora.note: These small kana attach to the kana before them and do not form their own mora (e.g. きゃ is 1 mora, not 2). Every other kana is its own mora, including ん, っ, and the long-vowel mark ー.

pitch.note: pitch is the standard accent number for the word's dictionary reading (as shown on kanshudo). Combined with the reading's mora split, it fully determines the word's high/low pitch pattern.

types.0: heiban (flat) — mora 1 is low, mora 2 through the end are high, and a following particle stays high.
types.1: atamadaka (head-high) — mora 1 is high, everything from mora 2 onward (including a following particle) is low.
types.N: nakadaka (N before the last mora) or odaka (N equals the last mora) — mora 1 is low, mora 2 through N are high, then it drops after mora N. Odaka sounds identical to heiban in isolation, but a following particle drops in pitch, unlike heiban.
types.null: no pitch accent data available for this word

jlpt.null: not part of the JLPT vocabulary lists

readingPhenomena.note: Why a word is shown with more than one accepted pronunciation (pronunciationSplit in words.json) — these are the recognized causes, not separate dictionary readings. Rendered as a summary banner at the top of a kanji's info popup (buildInfoButton, main.js) whenever one of its words has a tagged variant.

counterSuffix.label: counter suffix
counterSuffix.note: A counter is a suffix attached to a number to count objects of a particular kind (e.g. 本 for long cylindrical objects, 人 for people). Some counters shift pronunciation depending on the number they follow.

hanDakuonka.label: 半濁音化
hanDakuonka.note: han-dakuon-ka ("half-voicing") — an h-row reading (は/ひ/ふ/へ/ほ) shifts to its half-voiced p-row counterpart (ぱ/ぴ/ぷ/ぺ/ぽ), most often after a small っ in a counter or compound. E.g. 本 (ほん) → 一本 (いっぽん).

rendaku.label: 連濁
rendaku.note: rendaku ("sequential voicing") — the initial consonant of a compound's second element voices (k→g, s→z, t→d, h→b) when preceded by the first element. E.g. 人 (ひと) → 殺人 (さつじん).

onbin.label: 音便
onbin.note: onbin ("euphonic change") — a mora contracts or shifts for ease of pronunciation in a compound, most often to a small っ (促音便) or to ん (撥音便). E.g. 一 (いち) + 本 → 一本 (いっぽん).

variantTypes.note: What each tagged glyph in kanji.json's variants list actually is, shown in the variant-comparison popup (click a variant's parenthetical tag). Keyed by the variant glyph itself; `standard` describes the card's own kanji on the other side of the comparison.
